## Cryptography

The signature and encryption schemes, and whether the mathematics is done (real) or only charged for (modelled). Committees, where t-of-n servers share one authority's key, are a research option and not the US system.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-envelope"></span>`security.envelope` | string | | `ieee1609.2` | `ieee1609.2`, `etsi103097`<br>recommended ieee1609.2 (US). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The envelope profile: `ieee1609.2` or `etsi103097`. The secured-message format: IEEE 1609.2 (the US) or ETSI TS 103 097 (Europe). |
| <span id="s-security-signature"></span>`security.signature` | string | | `ecdsa-p256` | `ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1`, `ecdsa-p384`, `hybrid-falcon512-ecdsa-p256`, `hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256`, `hybrid-mldsa65-ecdsa-p256`, `ml-dsa-44`, `ml-dsa-65`, `ml-dsa-87`, `falcon-512`, `falcon-1024`, `slh-dsa-sha2-128s`, `slh-dsa-sha2-128f`<br>narrowed by `security.crypto_mode` when real<br>recommended ECDSA P-256, or a hybrid to study the cost of post-quantum security. | basic | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | The signature scheme, e.g. `ecdsa-p256`, `hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256`, `ml-dsa-65` — any id in `v2xw_sec::scheme::SIGNATURE_IDS`. The digital signature on every message. ECDSA is what is deployed today; post-quantum signatures resist a quantum computer but are many times larger. *Status: Any scheme in the registry (v2xw_sec::scheme::SIGNATURE_IDS; adding one is one module): classical ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1, ecdsa-p384; hybrids (ECDSA P-256 with Falcon-512, ML-DSA-44 or ML-DSA-65 concatenated); pure ML-DSA-44/65/87, Falcon-512/1024 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s/128f. Each changes the octets of every signed message and attached certificate on the air by its parts' published sizes (FIPS 204, FIPS 205, Falcon, SEC 1; a pure scheme replaces the ECDSA fields); an SPDU above the network MTU is refused and counted unless a fragmenter is selected. Each is charged its time: every signature and verification costs the sum of its parts on the hardware profile, a profile with no figure for a part falls back to the catalogue anchor it names (crypto_anchors; derived by cycle ratio where nothing is published, and flagged), and a profile that prices none is refused by name (the reference OBU publishes no post-quantum figure). brainpool and P-384 are charged the P-256 time. Only ecdsa-p256 runs in real crypto mode. A post-quantum scheme is the credential system's too (SCMS and CCMS): every certificate carries the post-quantum key and issuer signature, every signed backend message the post-quantum signature, authorities pay at the Raspberry Pi 5 liboqs figure (an upper bound for a server) and devices at the Cohda MK6's; there is no post-quantum butterfly, so a device generates one post-quantum key per pseudonym certificate or ticket and uploads each encrypted to the PCA or AA (v2xw_proto::hybrid).* |

How a certificate response is encrypted to its device: ECIES on P-256 (IEEE 1609.2), or a post-quantum or hybrid scheme for study. |

## Deployment

Which certificate system runs and how it is laid out: the providers on the trust list, the electors who sign that list, and the parts of the design the US does not deploy. Leave it on "US system (2025)" for the real deployment. Any change the US does not make is marked not US and recorded in the run's manifest.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-protocol-id"></span>`security.protocol.id` | string | | | `protocol/etsi/ts102941`, `protocol/scms/camp` (or another value)<br>recommended The one that matches the message format. | basic | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | The model's registry id. Which credential system issues the certificates vehicles sign with: the US Security Credential Management System (SCMS) or the European C-ITS trust model (ETSI TS 102 941). *Status: 'protocol/scms/camp' runs the credential lifecycle; its params set i_period_s (default one week), cert_lifetime_s (the period plus an hour), certs_per_period (20), pool_periods (2 held at the start), topup_below_periods (1), cert_shuffle_threshold (1,000) and cert_shuffle_window_s (2 days, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67; Brecht's 10,000 or one day as a setting), report_shuffle_threshold (10,000) and report_shuffle_window_s (one day, SCMS-765): a batch closes at the count or the window, whichever comes first; crl_cadence_s (one day; 0 publishes on decision), crl_fetch_interval_s (3600, an ASSUMPTION inside CAMP's weekly bound) and crl_broadcast_interval_s (5, the longest USDOT RSU v4.1 Store and Repeat interval). Every default's source: docs/reference/scms-constants.md. Vehicles top up over their backend link when the pool runs low and cannot sign once it is empty. 'protocol/etsi/ts102941' runs the ETSI ITS PKI: authorization tickets (certs_per_period a period, no linkage), TS 103 759 reports straight to the MA, and passive revocation only — the authority's decision blocklists the enrolment credential at the EA, the vehicle keeps its tickets until they expire and no reception is refused (TS 102 941 §6.1.4 NOTE 4). It needs security.envelope 'etsi103097'; etsi_butterfly: 1 tops up with one butterfly authorization and a batch download (TS 102 941 V2 §6.2.3.5) instead of a request per ticket, and the AA never sees the enrolment identity. SCMS only: every vehicle is bootstrapped through the DCM with the electors' trust list and the RA's policy and chain files; enrolment_lifetime_s (six years, CAMP 1.2.2) with reenrol_lead_s (18 months, SM-REENR) renews it through the RA, no overlap; max_periods_ahead (156) caps what the RA provisions; a blocklisted or expired enrolment is refused its top-up. ETSI only: the TLM signs one ECTL and the Root CA one CA-CRL at the start, and every station fetches both from the Distribution Centre (the CPOC) when it joins and then every crl_fetch_interval_s, over its own access, receiving only what is newer (TS 102 941 §6.3.3); nothing re-issues either list during a run.* |

| <span id="s-security-scms-crl-poll"></span>`security.scms.crl_poll` | string | | `conditional` | `conditional`, `info-status`<br>recommended conditional (today's default); info-status for the two-step fetch IEEE 1609.2.1 defines. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How a cellular vehicle polls its RA for new revocation lists: `conditional` (default), the composite CRL with `If-Modified-Since`, one exchange; `info-status`, the RA's signed certificate-management information status first (IEEE 1609.2.1 §6.3.5.14, also `If-Modified-Since`), and the composite CRL only when it holds an older list: two exchanges on a change, and the status's bytes on the air. How a cellular vehicle checks its RA for new revocation lists each hour. conditional: it asks for the whole composite list and gets a short 'not modified' when nothing changed. info-status: it first fetches the RA's signed status of its lists, CTL and authority certificates (IEEE 1609.2.1 6.3.5.14), and downloads the list only if it holds an older one, which costs a second exchange when something did change. |

## Receiver checks

What a receiving vehicle accepts: how old or how far in the future a message may be, and which messages it verifies when it cannot verify all of them.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-verification-policy"></span>`security.verification_policy` | string | | `verify-all` | `verify-all`, `on-demand`, `prioritized`<br>recommended Verify every message, unless you study verification load. With detection on, expect a warning for any other choice. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `verify-all`, `on-demand` or `prioritized`. Which received messages a vehicle checks the signature of. Checking everything is safest but can overload the security chip in dense traffic. Misbehaviour detection only judges messages whose signature was checked (a report's evidence is the accused's signed messages, SCMS Manager SM-MBR v1.0 §2.3.1.2.1), so verifying on demand or nearest first also blinds detection: in testing, on-demand cut reports from 897 to 79 and no attacker was revoked. |
| <span id="s-security-on-demand-threshold"></span>`security.on_demand_threshold` | number | score | | (0, 1]<br>recommended 0.5 (a time to collision of 1 s); 0.05 to 0.9. No published operating point (Krishnan &amp; Weimerskirch 2011); sweep it. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The relevance score at or above which an `on-demand` node verifies a message from a signer it already knows. 0.5 unless set; refused under any other policy. Under on-demand verification, how threatening a known vehicle's message must look (from its time to collision, 0 to 1) before it is checked; lower checks more messages and costs more processor time. Applies when `security.verification_policy` is `on-demand`. |
| <span id="s-security-prioritized-horizon-m"></span>`security.prioritized_horizon_m` | number | m | | [10, 2000]<br>recommended 300 m (the DSRC/C-V2X awareness range); 100 to 1000 m. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The distance beyond which proximity adds nothing to a `prioritized` node's service priority, metres. 300 unless set; refused under any other policy. Under prioritized verification, how far away a sender can be and still be checked ahead of farther ones; senders beyond it get no head start for being near. Applies when `security.verification_policy` is `prioritized`. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-rx-beacon-max-age-s"></span>`security.scms.rx_beacon_max_age_s` | number | s | `30.0` | [0, 31536000]<br>recommended By profile: 30 s in the US (SAE J2945/1 Table 11, the BSM validity period), 2 s in Europe (CAR 2 CAR Communication Consortium Basic System Profile RS_BSP_168); a year turns the check off for a study. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The receiver's `generationTime` relevance window (IEEE 1609.2 §5.2, `v2xw_node::rxval::GenerationTimeWindow`): the oldest a received BSM, CAM, PSM or VAM may be on the receiver's own clock, seconds. Unset, by profile (`crate::credentials::generation_window`): 30 under the US IEEE 1609.2 envelope (SAE J2945/1 Table 11), 2 under ETSI (C2C-CC BSP RS_BSP_168). Older ones are discarded unverified and never reach a detector. How old a received safety beacon (BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM) may be, by the receiver's own clock, before it is thrown away unchecked (IEEE 1609.2 relevance check). It makes an old replay harmless, and it is why a vehicle whose clock is badly wrong is ignored rather than reported for misbehaviour. Left unset it follows the profile: 30 s in the US, 2 s in Europe. Under the US window a replay a few seconds old is verified and must be caught by misbehaviour detection. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-rx-max-age-s"></span>`security.scms.rx_max_age_s` | number | s | `600.0` | [0, 31536000]<br>recommended 600 s (RS_BSP_168). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The same for every other application message (SPaT, MAP, DENM, CPM, SRM, SSM), seconds (600 unless set, RS_BSP_168, under either profile). The same age limit for every other application message: signal phase, intersection maps, hazard warnings, collective perception. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-rx-max-future-s"></span>`security.scms.rx_max_future_s` | number | s | `30.0` | [0, 31536000]<br>recommended By profile: 30 s in the US (SAE J2945/1 Table 11, the acceptable future data period), 0.04 s in Europe (RS_BSP_168); a year turns the check off for a study. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How far ahead of the receiver's own clock a `generationTime` may be, seconds. Unset, by profile: 30 under the US envelope (J2945/1 Table 11), 0.04 under ETSI (RS_BSP_168). How far ahead of the receiver's own clock a message's time stamp may be. A sender whose clock runs ahead is ignored past it. Left unset it follows the profile: 30 s in the US, 40 ms in Europe. The misbehaviour authority still sets aside report evidence stamped more than 40 ms after its report, whatever this says. |

## Certificate lifecycle

How a vehicle gets and uses its certificates. It enrols once, receives 20 pseudonym certificates per week in batches from the RA, tops up before it runs out, and changes pseudonym while driving so it cannot be followed. Defaults are the US deployment's, with the source on each field.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-signer-id-policy-full-cert-every-ms"></span>`security.signer_id_policy.full_cert_every_ms` | integer | ms | | [0, 3600000]<br>recommended Unset (BSM 450 ms, SAE J2945/1 6.5.2 vMaxCertDigestInterval; CAM 1 s, ETSI TS 103 097). A value overrides both. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The cadence, milliseconds, for every message type. Unset, each message type takes its own standard's: a BSM attaches its certificate when 450 ms have passed since the last one that did (SAE J2945/1 §6.5.2 `BSMSIGN-003`, Table 21 `vMaxCertDigestInterval`), a CAM and every other message once a second (ETSI TS 103 097 §7.1.1). A value overrides both; 0 attaches it to every message. How often a message carries the full certificate rather than an 8-byte digest; receivers need the certificate once to verify the digests. Unset, each message type takes its standard's: a BSM every 450 ms, a CAM once a second. |
| <span id="s-security-signer-id-policy-digest-otherwise"></span>`security.signer_id_policy.digest_otherwise` | boolean | | `true` | recommended On. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Attach a digest the rest of the time. Send an 8-byte certificate digest between full certificates, which saves about 140 bytes a message. |
| <span id="s-security-signer-id-policy-on-new-neighbour"></span>`security.signer_id_policy.on_new_neighbour` | boolean | | | recommended Off (the US cadence alone); on for the ETSI rule (TS 103 097 §7.1.1). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Also attach the certificate to the next BSM or CAM after a station this node has not heard before appears (the ETSI CAM rule, TS 103 097 V1.3.1 §7.1.1). Off by default, and left out of a scenario that does not set it. Send the full certificate in the next safety message whenever a vehicle it has not heard before comes into range, so the newcomer can check its signatures at once. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-strategy"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.strategy` | string | | `by-region` | `by-region`, `time`, `distance`, `j2945-1`, `nyc-pilot`, `c2c-cc`, `mix-zone`, `silent`<br>recommended By region (US: SAE J2945/1). Time-based only to study the change rate itself. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `by-region` (the default), `time`, `distance`, `j2945-1`, `nyc-pilot`, `c2c-cc`, `mix-zone` or `silent` (`crate::pseudonym_policy`). `by-region` is the rule of the envelope's region (`PseudonymChangeSpec::effective_strategy`). When a vehicle switches to a new anonymous certificate, so an eavesdropper cannot follow it across the city. The default follows the region: SAE J2945/1 in the US (every 5 minutes, but not within 2,100 m of the last change or during hard braking or an ABS event), every 5 minutes in Europe. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-period-s"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.period_s` | number | s | | [1, 86400]<br>recommended 60 to 300 s; 300 s is SAE J2945/1's interval. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The period, seconds, when the strategy is time-based. How often a vehicle changes pseudonym under the time-based strategy. Applies when `security.pseudonym_change.strategy` is `time`. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-distance-m"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.distance_m` | number | m | | [1, 100000]<br>recommended 2,000 m (the NYC pilot); 2,100 m is SAE J2945/1's vCertChangeDistance, which the j2945-1 strategy applies on its own. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The distance, metres, when the strategy is distance-based. Under the distance strategy, how far in a straight line from the last change point a vehicle must be before it changes pseudonym. Applies when `security.pseudonym_change.strategy` is `distance`. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-silent-period-s"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.silent_period_s[]` | number | s | | [0, 60]<br>recommended None; 3 to 13 s (PRESERVE) for a privacy study. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A random silence after each pseudonym change, between from and to seconds, so a listener loses the vehicle; its safety messages stop too. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-mix-zone-radius-m"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.mix_zone_radius_m` | number | m | | [5, 500]<br>recommended 30 m (one junction, Freudiger et al. 2007). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The mix zone's radius around a signalised intersection, metres (`mix-zone`). Under the mix-zone strategy, the radius of the zone at a signalised junction where vehicles change pseudonym together. Applies when `security.pseudonym_change.strategy` is `mix-zone`. |
| <span id="s-security-pseudonym-change-mix-zone-min-age-s"></span>`security.pseudonym_change.mix_zone_min_age_s` | number | s | | [0, 3600]<br>recommended 60 s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The age a pseudonym must reach before a mix zone changes it, seconds (`mix-zone`). The youngest pseudonym a mix zone changes, so a vehicle does not burn certificates at every junction. Applies when `security.pseudonym_change.strategy` is `mix-zone`. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-i-period-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.i_period_s` | number | s | `604800.0` | [1, 31536000]<br>recommended 604,800 s (one week, CAMP-EE) on the real calendar; 60 to 3,600 s only with time.calendar compressed. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The i-period, s: how long one set of pseudonym certificates is current (one week, 604,800 s, CAMP-EE §2.1.5.3.2). Anything shorter needs `time.calendar: compressed`. How long one set of pseudonym certificates is current. The US system uses one week from its 2015-01-06 epoch; a shorter period compresses the calendar so a short run sees weekly events, and the run is then labelled compressed. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-cert-lifetime-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.cert_lifetime_s` | number | s | `608400.0` | [1, 31536000]<br>recommended 608,400 s (the week plus one hour, CAMP-EE); at least the i-period. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A pseudonym certificate's lifetime, s: the i-period plus the overlap (10,140 min, one hour longer than the week, CAMP-EE §2.1.5.3.2). How long each pseudonym certificate is valid: the period plus an overlap, so a vehicle always holds a valid one across the change of week. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-certs-per-period"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.certs_per_period` | integer | certificates | `20` | [1, 60]<br>recommended 20 (the US profile); 5 to 60 (60 for vehicles that change often, such as taxis). | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Pseudonym certificates per i-period, all valid at once (20, CAMP-EE Table 2.1.2.6.2; at most 60). How many pseudonym certificates a vehicle may use in one week, all valid at once. More lets it change identity more often without reusing one, at the cost of bigger downloads, and one revocation then covers more certificates. The US profile issues 20 a week (CAMP-EE Table 2.1.2.6.2). |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-pool-periods"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.pool_periods` | integer | i-periods | `2` | [1, 64]<br>recommended 2 (engine default); 1 to 8 (a THEA device is pre-loaded with three years, more than any run uses). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | i-periods a vehicle holds when the run starts (2). How many weeks of certificates a vehicle holds when the run starts. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-topup-below-periods"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.topup_below_periods` | integer | i-periods | `1` | [0, 64]<br>recommended 1 (engine default); 0 to 4. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A vehicle asks for its next period when fewer than this many periods, the current one counted, remain (1; 0 turns top-ups off). A vehicle asks for its next week of certificates when fewer than this many weeks, the current one counted, remain; 0 turns top-ups off, so the pool only drains. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-max-periods-ahead"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.max_periods_ahead` | integer | i-periods | `156` | [1, 520]<br>recommended 156 weeks (three years, CAMP Primer); 1 to 156. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The most i-periods ahead the RA provisions a device (156, three years, CAMP Primer p.7: 3,120 = 156 × 20). The most weeks ahead the Registration Authority provisions a device; a request for more is cut to this. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-cert-shuffle-threshold"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.cert_shuffle_threshold` | integer | requests | `1000` | [1, 1000000]<br>recommended 1,000 (CAMP's production value); 10 to 10,000 (Brecht et al. 2018 used 10,000). It acts on a device's first request only: every vehicle in a run is provisioned before it joins, and its weekly top-ups are the RA's pre-generation, which does not wait in this mix, so a run's results do not change. | advanced | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | Certificate requests that release the RA's shuffle before its window closes (1,000, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67 `shuffle_threshold`). How many certificate requests the Registration Authority collects and mixes before passing them on, so the authority that signs the certificates cannot tell which vehicle asked when; a batch also leaves when its oldest request reaches the shuffle window. CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2, Table 67. *Status: The RA's request shuffle acts on a device's first certificate request (CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67). Every vehicle in a run is provisioned before it joins (Phase2::provision, ScmsRun::preload), and its weekly top-ups are the RA's pre-generation, which goes to the ACA at the period boundary without waiting in this shuffle (CAMP Primer p.6), so a same-seed run is identical. Whether the board's review delay comes before an EAC vote. How a replaced elector's transition trust list is signed. Dual adds the outgoing elector's classical signature and the incoming elector's ML-DSA-65 signature, so a device that knows either key accepts it. The ML-DSA-65 half is modelled (its size and cost), not real. |

When the Electors' Advisory Committee replaces an elector: the first approved elector leaves, a new one joins, and a transition trust list is decided and published to every device. |

| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-root-termination-notice-at-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.root_termination_notice_at_s` | number | s | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended Unset; inside the run, with a fast-forward to reach a year, to study a provider leaving. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | When the peer provider gives notice of its termination, s into the run (absent: never): its root may not leave the trust list before 365 days have run ([SM-PROV] §3.5.6). Starts the 365-day notice before the provider's root may leave the trust list (SCMS Manager Provider Requirements §3.5.6): a removal of the peer provider's root voted before the notice has run is refused. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-test-ballot-interval-days"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.test_ballot_interval_days` | integer | days | `0` | [0, 730]<br>recommended Off for runs under a year; 365 (yearly, per Elector Policy) for longer runs. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How long an elector may go without signing before the Board holds a Test Ballot, days (absent or 0: no ballot is scheduled; 365 is Elector Policy v1.0 §1.1's "at least yearly"). How long electors may go without signing before a test ballot, in days: once one has, every elector signs the current trust list's contents to show its key still works. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-tls"></span>`security.scms.tls` | string | | `1.3` | `1.3`, `1.2`<br>recommended 1.3 (default); 1.2 to compare with older devices. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The TLS version of every device-to-RA session (`session-scmsAuth`, SCMS Manager EE profile §2.1.18: TLS 1.2 or 1.3): `1.3` (default) or `1.2`, whose handshake costs one more round trip before the first request. The TLS version a vehicle uses for its secure session with the Registration Authority over a cellular link. TLS 1.2 needs one more round trip to set up each session than TLS 1.3, so certificate requests and downloads start later. The US profile admits both (SCMS Manager EE profile 2.1.18). |

## Providers

The companies that run an SCMS. Each runs its own root, intermediate CA, RA, pseudonym CA, linkage authorities and MA. Names are neutral labels. Where each one's servers sit, and its share of vehicles, are assumptions, because no provider publishes them.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-scms-deployment-providers-name"></span>`security.scms.deployment.providers[].name` | string | | | `provider-a`, `provider-b`, `provider-c`, `provider-d`, `provider-e`, `provider-f` (or another value)<br>recommended A neutral label (provider-a, provider-b). | advanced | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | Its neutral label, e.g. `provider-b`. Which provider this row changes: one the preset names, or any name under Custom providers. *Status: The SCMS deployment (protocol/scms/camp only; refused otherwise). deployment.preset: us-production-2025 (default: two providers with neutral labels on one CTL signed by the five shared electors, quorum 3; each with its own offline root and ICA and its own ECA, RA, ACA (provider-b two), LA1, LA2, MA, CRL Generator and PG; no LOP, no CRL broadcast), us-test-ctl-2025 (the 2025-07-17 test CTL: six roots, five approved), camp-reference (the single SCMS with LOP and a central MA) or custom. providers[]: components, region (an ASSUMPTION; no provider publishes one), fleet_share (roadside units are split by it), on_ctl (off: a provider nobody trusts), ma_mode (manual-review with ma_review_s, or automatic) and crl_publication (sla-1-business-day, cadence, on-decision) for that provider's run only. latency region (great-circle distance at fibre_fraction of c plus per_link_ms, ASSUMPTION) or flat; options.lop (off: the proxy hop is transparent), options.butterfly (original only) and options.identification_certs (on: emergency vehicles sign SRMs under OBU identification certificates and pseudonyms permit no SRM). Every node trusts every root on the CTL and holds every such provider's chain. Each provider runs its own backend: vehicles and roadside units are split by fleet_share, every RA serves every provider's signed CRL, MAs share reports, the Backend view shows each provider's entities as &lt;provider&gt;/&lt;role&gt;, and a home root rollover re-certifies every peer's copy of the home hierarchy. Partial: extra ACA instances take no load.* |

## Misbehaviour authority

How reports of bad messages reach the MA and how the MA decides. Covers what a vehicle stores and uploads, how the RA shuffles reports, the MA's decision rule, and whether a person reviews each case. The US pilots used manual review.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |

Overrides `security.protocol.params.ma_review_s` for this provider only. ## Revocation

What happens after a device is judged misbehaving: how fast its provider publishes the revocation list (CRL), how often vehicles fetch it, and how a receiver treats a list that is overdue.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-security-scms-deployment-providers-crl-publication"></span>`security.scms.deployment.providers[].crl_publication` | string | | | `sla-1-business-day`, `cadence`, `on-decision`<br>recommended sla-1-business-day (US). | advanced | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | When its CRL Generator publishes after a decision: `sla-1-business-day` (the SCMS Manager SLA, the US default), `cadence` (the run's `crl_cadence_s`) or `on-decision`. When the provider publishes a revocation: within one business day (the SCMS Manager SLA), on a fixed cadence, or at once. *Status: The SCMS deployment (protocol/scms/camp only; refused otherwise). deployment.preset: us-production-2025 (default: two providers with neutral labels on one CTL signed by the five shared electors, quorum 3; each with its own offline root and ICA and its own ECA, RA, ACA (provider-b two), LA1, LA2, MA, CRL Generator and PG; no LOP, no CRL broadcast), us-test-ctl-2025 (the 2025-07-17 test CTL: six roots, five approved), camp-reference (the single SCMS with LOP and a central MA) or custom. providers[]: components, region (an ASSUMPTION; no provider publishes one), fleet_share (roadside units are split by it), on_ctl (off: a provider nobody trusts), ma_mode (manual-review with ma_review_s, or automatic) and crl_publication (sla-1-business-day, cadence, on-decision) for that provider's run only. latency region (great-circle distance at fibre_fraction of c plus per_link_ms, ASSUMPTION) or flat; options.lop (off: the proxy hop is transparent), options.butterfly (original only) and options.identification_certs (on: emergency vehicles sign SRMs under OBU identification certificates and pseudonyms permit no SRM). Every node trusts every root on the CTL and holds every such provider's chain. Each provider runs its own backend: vehicles and roadside units are split by fleet_share, every RA serves every provider's signed CRL, MAs share reports, the Backend view shows each provider's entities as &lt;provider&gt;/&lt;role&gt;, and a home root rollover re-certifies every peer's copy of the home hierarchy. Partial: extra ACA instances take no load.* |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-crl-cadence-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.crl_cadence_s` | number | s | | [0, 2592000]<br>recommended Unset (the business-day rule); 0 to 86,400 s (a daily list, the USDOT 2013 working assumption). | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A fixed CRL publication cadence, s. Absent: each provider's own rule (the US presets publish within one business day of a decision, SCMS Manager Provider Requirements §3.4.9). 0 publishes on decision. A fixed schedule for publishing the revocation list. Left unset, each provider follows its own rule: the US providers publish within one business day of a revocation decision (SCMS Manager Provider Requirements 3.4.9). 0 publishes the moment a decision is made. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-crl-fetch-interval-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.crl_fetch_interval_s` | number | s | `3600.0` | [0.1, 1209600]<br>recommended 3,600 s (one hour, an engine assumption inside CAMP's weekly bound); 60 to 86,400 s. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How often a cellular vehicle polls for a new CRL, s (3,600). How often a vehicle with a cellular link asks for a newer revocation list. Shorter means revoked senders are refused sooner, for more cellular traffic; CAMP requires at least one fetch a week. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-crl-broadcast-interval-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.crl_broadcast_interval_s` | number | s | `5.0` | [0.1, 3600]<br>recommended 5 s (the longest USDOT RSU v4.1 store-and-repeat interval); 1 to 60 s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How often a roadside unit with the `crl` role repeats the CRL over the air, s (5). How often a roadside unit carrying the revocation list repeats it over the air to vehicles in range; only roadside units with the crl role do this, and the US deployment does not use it. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-crl-background-entries"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.crl_background_entries` | integer | revocations | `0` | [0, 1000000]<br>recommended 0 (only this run's revocations); 10,000 for a list a few years old. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Earlier revocations already on the home provider's CRL when the run starts (0): a standing list makes every CRL download and lookup that much larger. Revocations already on the home provider's revocation list when the run starts, so every CRL download and lookup carries a list of realistic length. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-component-revoked"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked` | string | | `none` | `none`, `ica`, `pca`, `ra`, `eca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`<br>recommended None; the pseudonym CA to study a compromised CA (every pseudonym it issued is refused once the list arrives). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The SCMS component whose certificate a provider revokes during the run: `none` (absent), `ica`, `pca`, `ra`, `eca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma` or `crlg`. The certificate goes on the hash CRL of the `(cracaId, crlSeries)` it names (series 2 or 256, [SMP] Table 1), and receivers that install that list refuse what it signed. An SCMS component (a CA, the RA, a linkage authority, the MA or the CRL signer) whose certificate its provider revokes during the run. The certificate goes on the provider's component revocation list (series 2, or the root-signed series 256), and every device that installs that list refuses what the component signed. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-component-revoked-provider"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked_provider` | string | | | `provider-a`, `provider-b`, `provider-c`, `provider-d`, `provider-e`, `provider-f` (or another value)<br>recommended Unset (the home provider, the first of the deployment). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whose component `component_revoked` revokes: a provider of the deployment by name (absent: the home provider, the first). Which provider revokes its component, by name. Applies when `security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked` is `ica`, `pca`, `ra`, `eca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-lifecycle-component-revoked-at-s"></span>`security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked_at_s` | number | s | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended Inside the run, early enough for the next publication and download (one business day under the US rule). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | When the component revocation is decided, s into the run (needed with `component_revoked`). When, in seconds into the run, the provider decides the component revocation; it is published by the provider's revocation-list rule and reaches devices with their next list download. Applies when `security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked` is `ica`, `pca`, `ra`, `eca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-crl-overdue-tolerance-s"></span>`security.scms.crl_overdue_tolerance_s` | integer | s | `1209600` | [0, 31536000]<br>recommended 1,209,600 s (two weeks, CAMP's value); 0 to 2,419,200 s to study a delayed or blocked revocation list. The next list is due a week after each one (nextCrl), so the rule acts only in runs that span weeks of calendar time. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `overdue_CRL_tolerance` (CAMP SCMS 1.2.2 Table 67), seconds: how long past a CRL's `nextCrl` a device keeps trusting the certificates that CRL governs before it refuses every message they sign. Two weeks (1,209,600 s) unless set. How long after a revocation list said the next one would be out a vehicle keeps trusting the certificates that list covers. Past it, the vehicle refuses every message those certificates sign, so a vehicle cut off from new lists (by an attacker or a dead link) stops trusting its neighbours. CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2, Table 67, overdue_CRL_tolerance. |
| <span id="s-security-scms-crl-overdue-scope"></span>`security.scms.crl_overdue_scope` | string | | `craca` | `craca`, `all`<br>recommended craca (default); all to study the strict reading. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Which messages an overdue pseudonym CRL makes a device refuse (`v2xw_node::rxval::CrlOverdueScope`): `craca` (default), the signers whose CRACA is the overdue list's; `all`, every message while any held series-1 list is past `nextCrl` + the tolerance. CAMP SCMS 1.2.2 Table 67 has the device "rejecting all of them", which the sources leave to either reading. What a vehicle refuses once a revocation list it holds is overdue past the tolerance. craca: only messages from certificates that list covers (the same certificate authority); all: every message, as CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2 Table 67 has the device "rejecting all of them" and warning the driver. The sources leave both readings open; they differ only after a root or CRACA changeover, when a vehicle holds an old authority's list that is no longer renewed. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`security.envelope`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `ieee1609.2` | IEEE 1609.2 (US) | The secured-message format of the US SCMS. |
 | `etsi103097` | ETSI TS 103 097 (Europe) | The European profile of the same structure; required by the ETSI credential system. |

??? note "`security.signature`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `ecdsa-p256` | ECDSA P-256 | The signature every deployed V2X system uses today: 64-octet signatures. |
 | `ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1` | ECDSA brainpool P-256r1 | The European alternative curve; same size, charged the P-256 time. |
 | `ecdsa-p384` | ECDSA P-384 | A longer curve: 32 more octets per signature; costs the device's P-384 figure, or its P-256 one times the published P-384 / P-256 ratio. |
 | `hybrid-falcon512-ecdsa-p256` | Post-quantum hybrid: Falcon-512 + P-256 | Adds 666 octets per signature and 1,563 per certificate; needs a fragmenter and a profile with a Falcon figure. |
 | `hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256` | Post-quantum hybrid: ML-DSA-44 + P-256 | FIPS 204 Dilithium beside P-256: the largest messages; needs a fragmenter and a profile with an ML-DSA figure. |
 | `hybrid-mldsa65-ecdsa-p256` | Hybrid: ECDSA P-256 + ML-DSA-65 | Raw concatenation. The ML-DSA-65 time on Cortex-A and Cohda profiles is derived from ML-DSA-44 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. |
 | `ml-dsa-44` | Post-quantum: ML-DSA-44 | pk 1,312 B, sig 2,420 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. |
 | `ml-dsa-65` | Post-quantum: ML-DSA-65 | pk 1,952 B, sig 3,309 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. Cortex-A and Cohda times are derived from ML-DSA-44 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. |
 | `ml-dsa-87` | Post-quantum: ML-DSA-87 | pk 2,592 B, sig 4,627 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. Times derived as for ML-DSA-65. |
 | `falcon-512` | Post-quantum: Falcon-512 (FN-DSA) | pk 897 B, padded sig 666 B [PQClean falcon-padded-512]. Key generation is slow (tens of ms on a Cortex-A72), which matters with no butterfly. |
 | `falcon-1024` | Post-quantum: Falcon-1024 (FN-DSA) | pk 1,793 B, padded sig 1,280 B [PQClean falcon-padded-1024]. Cortex-A and Cohda times derived from Falcon-512 by the Cortex-M7 cycle ratio. |
 | `slh-dsa-sha2-128s` | Post-quantum: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s | pk 32 B, sig 7,856 B [FIPS 205 Table 2]; hash-based, so its security rests on SHA-2 alone. Signing takes about a second on a vehicle-class core: an authority scheme, not a V2V one. |
 | `slh-dsa-sha2-128f` | Post-quantum: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128f | pk 32 B, sig 17,088 B [FIPS 205 Table 2]: eight frames' worth of signature. |

??? note "`security.kem`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `ecies-p256` | ECIES P-256 (deployed today) | 33 B ephemeral point + 16 B wrapped AES-128 key + 16 B tag. |
 | `ml-kem-512` | Post-quantum: ML-KEM-512 | ciphertext 768 B, encapsulation key 800 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]. |
 | `ml-kem-768` | Post-quantum: ML-KEM-768 | ciphertext 1,088 B, encapsulation key 1,184 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]. |
 | `ml-kem-1024` | Post-quantum: ML-KEM-1024 | ciphertext 1,568 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]; times derived from ML-KEM-768 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. |
 | `hybrid-ecies-p256-ml-kem-768` | Hybrid: ECIES P-256 + ML-KEM-768 | Both encapsulations travel; no 1609.2 structure for it exists yet (derived). |

??? note "`security.threshold.protocol`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `frost-p256` | FROST threshold Schnorr (RFC 9591, P-256) | RFC 9591 §5, §6.4 (FROST(P-256, SHA-256): Ne = 33, Ns = 32) |
 | `cggmp21-ecdsa` | Threshold ECDSA (CGGMP21) — 1609.2-compatible output | CGGMP21, ePrint 2021/060 (non-interactive variant: 3 presign rounds + 1 online) |
 | `umbrella` | Umbrella authority: t-of-n umbrella credentials over k derived leaves | placeholder binding (owner's specification pending, brief §8.3) |
 | `shamir-feldman` | t-of-n secret release (Shamir + Feldman), for linkage seeds | Shamir 1979 secret sharing with Feldman 1987 verifiable shares (dealer model) |

??? note "`security.threshold.roles[]`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `pca` | Pseudonym CA | A committee of servers signs pseudonym certificates; no single server holds the key. |
 | `crl` | CRL Generator | A committee signs the revocation list. |
 | `linkage` | Linkage authorities | A t-of-n committee releases linkage seeds, so revoking a vehicle needs a quorum. |

??? note "`security.threshold.umbrella_inner`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `frost-p256` | FROST threshold Schnorr (RFC 9591, P-256) | RFC 9591 §5, §6.4 (FROST(P-256, SHA-256): Ne = 33, Ns = 32) |
 | `cggmp21-ecdsa` | Threshold ECDSA (CGGMP21) — 1609.2-compatible output | CGGMP21, ePrint 2021/060 (non-interactive variant: 3 presign rounds + 1 online) |
 | `umbrella` | Umbrella authority: t-of-n umbrella credentials over k derived leaves | Cannot sign its own umbrellas: choose a signing protocol for the umbrella certificates. |
 | `shamir-feldman` | t-of-n secret release (Shamir + Feldman), for linkage seeds | Shamir 1979 secret sharing with Feldman 1987 verifiable shares (dealer model) |

??? note "`security.crypto_mode`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `modeled` | Costed (fast) | Signing and verification take the hardware's measured time; the outcome is modelled. |
 | `real` | Computed (exact, slow) | Real ECDSA over real bytes. Only P-256 is available in this mode. |

??? note "`security.protocol.id`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `protocol/etsi/ts102941` | European CCMS (ETSI TS 102 941) | Authorization tickets, an enrolment authority and passive revocation. |
 | `protocol/scms/camp` | US SCMS (CAMP) | The US credential system: butterfly keys, two linkage authorities, linkage-value CRL. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.preset`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `us-production-2025` | US system (2025) | Two providers on one trust list, neutral labels a and b: the deployed US SCMS. |
 | `us-test-ctl-2025` | US test trust list (17 Jul 2025) | Six roots, five approved; provider-f's root ships but is not trusted. |
 | `camp-reference` | CAMP reference design | One SCMS with LOP, CRL Store, RSU broadcast and a central MA at flat latency: the pre-2025 topology, not the US system. |
 | `custom` | Custom providers | You list the providers below; each starts as a copy of a US provider. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.options.butterfly`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `original` | Original butterfly key expansion | The device sends signing and encryption caterpillar keys, the RA expands them into cocoon keys and the ACA encrypts each certificate to the device: the US profile. |
 | `unified` | Unified butterfly | Not deployed in the US: the US profile uses the original expansion only and the unified response key is unconfirmed, so this build refuses it. |
 | `cubk` | Compact unified butterfly | Not deployed in the US: the US profile uses the original expansion only and the compact unified response key is unconfirmed, so this build refuses it. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.latency`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `region` | Distance-based | Great-circle distance between server sites at fibre speed, plus a fixed overhead per link (an assumption). |
 | `flat` | Fixed latency | Every backend link takes the backend network's fixed latency, wherever the servers are. |

??? note "`security.scms.chain_file`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `all-providers` | Every provider's CA certificates | Each device holds the global chain file with every trusted provider's CAs, so it verifies any provider's vehicles at once. |
 | `home-provider` | Only my provider's | A device learns other providers' ICA and ACA over the air by P2PCD before it can verify their vehicles (an assumption). |

??? note "`security.scms.crl_poll`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `conditional` | Revocation list, if changed (one exchange) | The vehicle asks the RA for its composite revocation list with If-Modified-Since: the list when it changed, a short 412 when not. |
 | `info-status` | Status file first, then what changed | The vehicle first fetches the RA's signed status of its lists (IEEE 1609.2.1 6.3.5.14), then downloads the revocation list only if it holds an older one. |

??? note "`security.verification_policy`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `verify-all` | Verify every message | Every received message is verified, whatever it costs the security module. |
 | `on-demand` | Verify on demand | Only messages an application is about to act on are verified. Misbehaviour detection runs only on verified messages, so detection goes nearly blind (897 reports fell to 79 in testing). |
 | `prioritized` | Verify nearest first | When the module cannot keep up, the closest and most relevant senders are verified first. |

??? note "`security.pseudonym_change.strategy`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `by-region` | By region (US: SAE J2945/1) | The region's own rule: SAE J2945/1 CERTCHG under the US IEEE 1609.2 envelope, every 5 minutes under ETSI. A scenario that sets period_s gets the time rule. |
 | `time` | Every few minutes (time only) | Change certificate after period_s of use (300 s unless set), however close the vehicle is to the last change point. |
 | `distance` | Every few kilometres (NYC pilot) | Change once the vehicle is distance_m in a straight line from the last change point; the NYC Connected Vehicle Pilot used 2 km. |
 | `j2945-1` | SAE J2945/1 (5 min unless within 2,100 m of the last change; not during a critical event) | Change once 5 minutes have passed and the vehicle is at least 2,100 m in a straight line from the last change point (vCertChangeDistance), and never while its BSM carries a critical event flag (CERTCHG-001, -002); an expiring certificate still changes. |
 | `nyc-pilot` | NYC CV pilot (2 km or 5 min) | Change at 2 km in a straight line from the last change point or after 5 minutes, whichever comes first. |
 | `c2c-cc` | European car makers' rule (C2C-CC) | After 0.8-1.5 km, then 0.8 km plus 2-6 minutes, then every 10-35 km. |
 | `mix-zone` | In mix zones at junctions | Change inside a zone around each signalised junction, where many vehicles mingle. |
 | `silent` | Never (keep one identity) | No change: the baseline a tracker finds easiest. |

??? note "`security.scms.lifecycle.ctl_genesis_sequence`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `auto` | By date, as the production series | Sequence 1 when the run starts on or after 2025-07-16 (the live production trust list), 0 before. |
 | `0` | 0 | The first production trust list's number (2019-12-12), whatever the run's date. |
 | `1` | 1 | The live production trust list's number (effective 2025-07-16), whatever the run's date. |

??? note "`security.scms.lifecycle.eac_review`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | The times given are the votes | The rollover and removal times are when the electors vote. |
 | `elector-policy` | The times given are requests; the board reviews per Elector Policy | Each time is a request; the vote follows 10 business days later for an addition and 24 hours later for a removal. |

??? note "`security.scms.lifecycle.elector_replacement_pq`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `off` | Classical keys | A replaced elector's transition trust list is signed by the remaining P-384 electors only. |
 | `dual` | Dual signatures (classical + ML-DSA-65) | The outgoing elector's P-384 key and the incoming elector's ML-DSA-65 key both sign the transition trust list. |

??? note "`security.scms.tls`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |

 | `1.2` | TLS 1.2 | One more round trip than TLS 1.3 before the first request; also allowed by the EE profile. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.providers[].ica_levels`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `1` | One intermediate CA (US) | Root, one ICA, then the issuing CAs, as every US provider runs. |
 | `2` | 2 intermediate CAs (not US) | A deeper hierarchy, each level issued by the one above, every level in the chain file; the run is then not the US system and each chain is one certificate longer per level. |
 | `3` | 3 intermediate CAs (not US) | A deeper hierarchy, each level issued by the one above, every level in the chain file; the run is then not the US system and each chain is one certificate longer per level. |
 | `4` | 4 intermediate CAs (not US) | A deeper hierarchy, each level issued by the one above, every level in the chain file; the run is then not the US system and each chain is one certificate longer per level. |
 | `5` | 5 intermediate CAs (not US) | A deeper hierarchy, each level issued by the one above, every level in the chain file; the run is then not the US system and each chain is one certificate longer per level. |
 | `6` | 6 or more (refused) | A receiver accepts at most 8 certificates in a chain (IEEE 1609.2), and root, 6 levels, the ACA and the pseudonym certificate are 9. |

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `manual-review` | An operator reviews each case | The CV-pilot "minimum viable" MA: a person reviews the evidence before a revocation (CAMP 1.2.2 §4.2-4.3). |
 | `automatic` | Acted on at once | The MA revokes as soon as its rule decides, with no human review. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.providers[].ma_policy`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `cv-pilot-manual` | CV-pilot operator review (US default) | Today's MA: reports corroborated into events (2 reporters an event, 3 events in 60 s, 3 reporters), then an operator's 8 h review, as the CV pilots ran it (CAMP122 §4.2-4.3); on a compressed calendar the review is automatic, as today. The evidence rule is an ASSUMPTION. |
 | `corroborated-auto` | Corroborated, automatic | The same corroborating rule with no operator: it revokes as soon as the evidence suffices. |
 | `legacy-window` | Legacy persistence gate | The legacy corpus's rule (3 trusted reporters over 4 distinct seconds spanning 3 s inside 15 s), kept for parity with its results; automatic. |
 | `pseudonym-k` | k reporters per certificate | Revokes a pseudonym certificate once k different reporters accused it (k = 3, no trust gate; v2xw ma-replay's rule); k = 1 lets one report revoke (unsound). Automatic. |
 | `device-k` | k reporters per device | Revokes a whole device, linked through the linkage authorities, once k different reporters accused any of its certificates within 1 h (k = 3; v2xw ma-replay's rule). Automatic. |
 | `catch` | Accuracy-aware (CaTch-style) | Per device, each reporter counts only the share of the position error the accused's own stated accuracy cannot explain; revokes at a summed score of 3 within 1 h (Kamel et al., IEEE WCNC 2019). Automatic. |
 | `cluster` | Population guard | Per device, 3 reporters within 1 h; when 3 devices of one class are accused at once, a device of that class needs 3 times the reporters, so one product line's benign trigger cannot revoke the line. Automatic. |
 | `custom` | Custom | Starts from the US default's values; every field you write is yours. |

??? note "`security.scms.ma_policy.identity`"

??? note "`security.scms.ma_policy.evidence.accuracy_weighting`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | None | Every report counts in full, whatever accuracy the accused stated. |
 | `catch` | Discount what stated accuracy explains | A position report counts only the deviation the accused's own stated accuracy cannot explain (CaTch); other checks count in full. |

??? note "`security.scms.ma_policy.decay.mode`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | None | Evidence keeps its score until it leaves the window. |
 | `daily-multiplier` | Daily multiplier (SCMS Manager MBR v1.0) | Once a day, at the hour set (05:00 Eastern unless set), every report's score is multiplied by the factor (0.9 unless set), as the US device's report store does. Acts on the score threshold. |
 | `half-life` | Half-life | A report's score halves every half-life (1 day unless set), continuously. Acts on the score threshold. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.providers[].crl_publication`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sla-1-business-day` | Within one business day | The provider publishes a revocation within one business day of the decision (SCMS Manager service-level agreement). |
 | `cadence` | On a fixed cadence | The CRL is published on the fixed cadence set under Revocation, as in the CAMP reference design. |
 | `on-decision` | As soon as decided | The CRL is re-signed and published the moment the MA decides. |

??? note "`security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | No component revoked | No SCMS component certificate is revoked during the run. |
 | `ica` | Intermediate CA | The ICA's certificate goes on the root-signed list; every certificate under it stops verifying. Not available on an S2X provider (no certificate signs its list). |
 | `pca` | Pseudonym CA (ACA) | The pseudonym CA's certificate goes on the component list; receivers that install it refuse every pseudonym it issued (issuer-revoked). |
 | `ra` | Registration Authority | The RA's certificate goes on the component list; devices refuse its signed responses. |
 | `eca` | Enrolment CA | The enrolment CA's certificate goes on the component list; the enrolment certificates it issued stop verifying. |
 | `la1` | Linkage Authority 1 | The first linkage authority's certificate goes on the component list. |
 | `la2` | Linkage Authority 2 | The second linkage authority's certificate goes on the component list. |
 | `ma` | Misbehaviour Authority | The MA's certificate goes on the root-signed list; devices stop encrypting their reports to it. |
 | `crlg` | CRL Generator | The CRL signer's certificate goes on the root-signed list; the lists it signed after the install stop verifying. |

??? note "`security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked_provider`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `provider-a` | provider-a | A provider of: US system (2025); US test trust list (17 Jul 2025); CAMP reference design. Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |
 | `provider-b` | provider-b | A provider of: US system (2025); US test trust list (17 Jul 2025). Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |
 | `provider-c` | provider-c | A provider of: US test trust list (17 Jul 2025). Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |
 | `provider-d` | provider-d | A provider of: US test trust list (17 Jul 2025). Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |
 | `provider-e` | provider-e | A provider of: US test trust list (17 Jul 2025). Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |
 | `provider-f` | provider-f | A provider of: US test trust list (17 Jul 2025). Under Custom providers any name may be typed. |

??? note "`security.scms.crl_overdue_scope`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `craca` | Only certificates under the overdue list | While a CRL is overdue, refuse only messages whose certificates that CRL's issuer covers (the default). |
 | `all` | Every message | While any series-1 CRL is overdue, refuse every message; CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67 allows either reading. |

??? note "`security.scms.deployment.providers[].capacity.*.service`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `mmc` | Workers in parallel (M/M/c) | Each request goes to the first free worker, as today's backend serves (ASSUMPTION: no provider publishes how its servers are pooled). |
 | `fifo-1` | One at a time (M/M/1) | One worker serves requests in arrival order; the same as workers: 1. |
